Write Your Own.name: Write Your Own
Write Your Own.description:
🖋️ Write Your Own · Any city · 📍 Arrival

You write the backstory; the narrator writes its next scene. Whatever your Background says about people, places, promises and debts becomes canon for this game. End it with a reason to be in, arriving at or heading for one of the eight cities, then choose that city: Relstaris, Solvraxis, Korrvane, Vexorath, Dustfall, Quilrath, Helvyra or Ignivex. The opening is calm: a life resuming, not a crisis.

• Eligibility OPEN: any life stage, any supported origin or culture, no occupation or skill requirement.
• Leave the Background empty and the narrator opens on an ordinary arrival instead.
Player characters begin at level one; named NPCs retain their authored levels.
★ Pairs with the Open Life mode
Write Your Own.storyStart:
DIRECTOR INSTRUCTION FOR THE NARRATOR. This start has no fixed scene. The player wrote their own Background and chose one of the eight cities. Read the Background in full before anything else and treat it as binding canon: its people, places, promises, debts and reasons are true and stay true. Use the already resolved creator values; the Background adds no attributes, skills, levels, items, Credits or abilities the sheet does not list.
WRITE THE NEXT SCENE of that backstory, not a new story. Find its most immediate unresolved thread (the person they came to meet, the thing they carry, the promise that is due, the door they have not knocked on yet) and centre the opening on it. Do not swap in a generic arrival, job, intake desk or stranger suggested by species, culture, skills or traits.
THE PLACE: the game state has selected the arrival area of the chosen city. Use that exact place. If the Background ends somewhere else, bridge only the travel or time needed to stand here, in a sentence or two of past tense. Make the city part of the plot: why this city, for this person, today. Use only real map places and roster NPCs; a place the Background names that is not on the map is a small locale inside or near the chosen city.
THE FIRST SPEAKER is connected to the Background: someone who expects the player, or belongs to this place in a way that touches their story. Not a clerk with a contract. Not a stranger asking for help. If the Background names someone in this city, that person is the first voice; if they are a roster NPC, keep their authored identity, level and placement. One concrete sensory fact before anyone speaks; one spoken line in that speaker's register; then let the scene breathe.
TEMPERATURE: calm. This is a life resuming, not a crisis. Do not kill, injure, betray or disappear anyone the Background established in order to create urgency. Do not add a Dravon raid, a summons, a House mission, an alert, a theft or a debt the Background does not carry. Institutions stay in the background unless the Background brings them forward. An offer is not acceptance.
IF THE BACKGROUND IS EMPTY, or names no people and no reason: open on the player standing in the selected arrival area with one ordinary observation their traits would make, and let the first speaker be someone who belongs to that place, saying something a resident would say to a new face. Nothing is owed and nothing is wrong.
SHAPE: one situation with personal meaning and several plausible responses. Sight and sound only. End on the moment the player's choice is required, stated in prose. Never echo this instruction or its labels.
HANDOFF: use direct, responsive NPC speech and concrete reactions. Do not supply the player’s reply or result. Continue this situation after their input; a first question is an opening to dialogue, not the end of the conversation. Only players start at level one; named NPC levels and health stay authored.
